subject: Post-call recap: inference unit economics — open questions & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Mason <kmason@payfront.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: inference unit economics — open questions & next steps

Kyle — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view, plus a short list of open questions and proposed next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- Token/unit cost is the top gating factor for expanding LLM into transactional product flows (invoice auto-classify + fields extraction).
- Peak latency requirements for the UI path are 150–200ms p95; current spikes break flows for intensive batches.
- Current ops team is stretched maintaining custom batching logic and ad-hoc caching; visibility into per-route cost is limited.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Inference: in-house microservice running on AWS EC2 GPUs via a custom K8s operator (no managed endpoint).
- Orchestration: EKS with Karpenter for node scaling; Redis for short-term KV cache.
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra, but no token-level cost attribution linked to traces.

Quantitative signals you gave
- Monthly inference tokens (est): ~3.6B tokens across all products, with 60% of traffic concentrated in a single payments pipeline.
- Target unit-cost reduction objective: 40–60% vs current infra (CFO target for next FY).

Openness and constraints
- Quantization: engineering is open to 4-bit/8-bit experiments if quality delta < 1.5% on our key metrics.
- Batching/caching: willing to centralize prefix caching if it doesn’t increase tail latency beyond SLOs.
- Compliance: customer data in inference path must remain in our AWS account; any hosted solution requires VPC peering or Private deployment.

Open questions (please confirm / fill in where possible)
1) Can you share a 7-day sample of request size distribution (tokens per request) and typical concurrency during peak hours? This will let us size batching and KV cache parameters.
2) What SLA is acceptable for the pilot? Is 99.5% availability enough for the first 30 days?
3) Who is the procurement contact and preferred contract cadence (monthly PO vs. annual contract)?

Proposed next steps
- We will draft a 3-week POC plan that validates: (a) 30–50% unit-cost reduction via batching + quantization profile, (b) p95 latency stays within 200ms for UI path, (c) no material quality regression on your invoice extraction testset. Deliverable: POC scope doc + pilot cost model.
- You to send the sample token distribution + procurement contact for contracting logistics.
- Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with your infra lead next week (propose Thu 7/2 or Fri 7/3).

Attachments: attached I included a one-page POC template (POC_scope.pdf) and an empty pilot cost model (pilot_cost_model.xlsx) for your team to populate.

If any of the summary points are off, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the POC plan by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Mason <kmason@payfront.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: PayFront Procurement <procurement@payfront.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference unit economics — open questions & next steps

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. Mostly correct; a few clarifications inline below.

Quick clarifications
- Monthly tokens: 3.6B is an accurate working number; the payments pipeline alone is closer to 2.2B.
- Latency: 150–200ms p95 is correct for UI flows; we can tolerate 250ms for async backend enrichment.
- Quantization threshold: quality delta ideally <1% on our F1 for field extraction; 1.5% is our absolute max.

Answers to open questions
1) Request distribution: I can export a 7-day CSV from our request logs by EOD; it will include tokens/request and concurrency samples.
2) Pilot SLA: procurement prefers to keep a 30-day operational review — 99.5% availability is acceptable for the initial pilot.
3) Procurement: procurement@payfront.com is the right mailbox. Primary contact is Maria Chen (maria.chen@payfront.com). They prefer issuing a 30-day PO for the pilot.

Additional notes
- Our infra lead (Ben Ortiz) should join the technical kickoff — I’ll copy him on the scheduling reply.
- We’d like to see a short plan for how you’ll measure quality regression (testset, thresholds, rollback criteria).

Attaching the request-sample export will follow in a separate mail; procurement asked for a one-page SOW and a rough cost estimate before issuing a PO.

On the timing: Thu 7/2 AM (PST) works for Ben and me; if you can send a calendar invite I’ll get Ben added.

--
Kyle Mason
Head of Product, PayFront
kmason@payfront.com | +1 (646) 555-6677

Lauren
